name: classla
description: Read and edit the courses you teach in Classla: find assignments, write and revise questions, update autograder tests and due dates.

interface.longDescription:
Classla is where teachers build and run their courses: assignments with multiple-choice, fill-in-the-blank, free-response, math and coding questions, autograded coding work, and due dates per section.

Connect Classla to work on the courses you teach from ChatGPT. Ask ChatGPT to list your courses, find an assignment, summarize what it asks, write new questions, edit existing ones, update a coding question's autograder tests, or change due dates. New assignments are created unpublished; you publish them in Classla.

You choose what to allow when you connect:
- Read your courses and assignments
- Create and edit assignments
- Read student work (rosters, submissions and answers), which is off unless you turn it on

You can change these or disconnect at any time from Settings, Connected apps in Classla.

What it cannot do: publish an assignment, enter grades, delete an assignment, or change who is enrolled. When students have already started an assignment, Classla holds a change until you confirm it.

Requires a Classla teacher account that Classla has verified.
defaultPrompt: Find my loops assignment and summarize its questions
Create an assignment with three multiple-choice questions about for loops

positive.description: List the teacher's courses. The reviewer account teaches two courses.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT lists both courses, "AP CSA, Period 3 (Demo)" and "How to use Classla", with their join codes. Nothing is changed.

positive.description: Find an assignment by its exact title and summarize its questions.
positive.prompt: Find the "Unit 3: Loops" assignment in my AP CSA demo class and summarize its questions.
positive.expected_behavior: A summary of Unit 3: Loops: a multiple-choice question, a Parsons (code ordering) problem, a short-answer question and a coding (IDE) exercise, each described in a line or two. ChatGPT may use search or list_assignments to find it, fetch to read it, or get_block_details for detail. Nothing is changed.

positive.description: Create a new unpublished assignment with three multiple-choice questions. Safe to repeat: each run adds another unpublished copy.
positive.prompt: In my AP CSA demo class, create an assignment called "For Loops Check" with three multiple-choice questions about for loops.
positive.expected_behavior: A new assignment "For Loops Check" in AP CSA, Period 3 (Demo) with three multiple-choice questions (create_mcq is called three times), each with one correct answer. ChatGPT says it is unpublished and that the teacher publishes it in Classla. Students cannot see it.

positive.description: Change an assignment's course-wide due date to an exact date and time. Safe to repeat: it sets the same date again.
positive.prompt: Set the due date of "Methods practice" in my AP CSA demo class to October 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM Eastern time.
positive.expected_behavior: set_due_dates is called with course_due_date 2026-10-30T23:59:00-04:00. ChatGPT confirms the course-wide due date is now October 30, 2026, 11:59 PM Eastern, and the tool reports 24 students with due dates set; in Classla every student's due date for Methods practice shows October 30. If ChatGPT passes something that is not a date, the tool refuses with "is not a date ... Nothing was changed" and ChatGPT retries with an ISO date.

positive.description: Read every assignment in a course with its due date. Works with the default permissions (Read student work is not needed).
positive.prompt: List the assignments in my AP CSA demo class with their due dates.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT lists the six assignments (Start here, Unit 3: Loops, Boolean logic check, Unit 3 test, Loops review, Methods practice, plus any "For Loops Check" copies from the create case) with each one's course-wide due date. Start here has none. Methods practice shows October 30, 2026 if the due-date case ran, its earlier date otherwise. Nothing is changed.

negative.description: Publishing is not supported: there is no publish tool. ChatGPT should say the teacher publishes in Classla; the assignment stays unpublished.
negative.prompt: Publish "For Loops Check" in my AP CSA demo class to my students.

negative.description: Grading is not supported: there is no grading tool. ChatGPT should say it cannot enter or change grades and point to grading in Classla; no grade changes.
negative.prompt: Give every student 100 on the "Unit 3 test" in my AP CSA demo class.

negative.description: Deleting an assignment is not supported. delete_block must not be called (it removes one block, not an assignment). ChatGPT should say the teacher deletes assignments in Classla; Loops review is unchanged.
negative.prompt: Delete the "Loops review" assignment from my AP CSA demo class.

review.commerce_description: Classla does not sell products or process payments through ChatGPT.

publication.release_notes:
Resubmission after review.
- Privacy: every tool now returns only what the request needs. Internal and debug fields are gone from tool responses: no stored internal keys inside student answers, no raw settings, no account ids for people, no join codes or internal section ids in settings, and no raw error text from Google Classroom. The text under a teacher's PDF redaction is no longer sent.
- Our privacy policy (https://classla.org/privacy, "Connected AI Apps") now lists every category of data a connected app can receive, by permission, what it never receives (email addresses, usernames, passwords, IP addresses, devices, account ids), where it goes, what Classla keeps, and the teacher's controls.
- Students are referred to by a number per connection (#1, #2, and so on). A teacher can now give one student an extension by that number.
- Every tool states all four annotations explicitly, and each value matches what the tool does.
